newsitem.title: CANADA: DiamondWorks in new Angola diamond deal.
newsitem.headline: DiamondWorks in new Angola diamond deal.

text.p: DiamondWorks Ltd said Thursday that it acquired a 50 percent interest in the Yetwene diamond concession in Angola's Luanada Norte province.
DiamondWorks is already mining alluvial diamonds at its Luo concession in Angola.
It acquired the new stake through deals with Sociedade Mineira do Lucapa (SML), Sociedade Mineira e de Investimentos de Lunda SA and Zizania Holdings Ltd of Jersey.

Under the deal, DiamondWorks will issue one million shares to Zizania, pay Zizania US$10,000 a month for a year and pay a S M LUS$50,000 signing fee to SML. DiamondWorks is reimbursing Zizania US$398,000 for equipment and will advance all costs up to US$5 million to bring the property into production.
DiamondWorks becomes operator of the projet and will receive half of the profits from diamond mining and preferential payback of capital expenditures.
The concession covers about 550 square km and is expected to go into production in the third quarter.

About 20 percent of the property's alluvial gravels were explored in the early 1970s by Diamang, a former Angolan consortium that included De Beers Consolidated Mines Inc. Diamang estimated that the explored portion had an alluvial resource containing more than 750,000 carats of diamonds, DiamondWorks said.
Endiama, Angola's state diamond mining company, estimates 99 percent of the diamonds are gem quality and have an average value of US$280 a carat, it said.
"Only a small portion of the concession has been explored and DiamondWorks believes there is excellent potential to add to the estimated diamond resources," the company said.
The deal is subject to a due diligence review and regulatory approvals.
